newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli army wounds two Palestinians in West Bank.
newsitem.headline: Israeli army wounds two Palestinians in West Bank.

text.p: Israeli soldiers shot two Palestinian school boys with rubber bullets on Monday during clashes in the West Bank, witnesses said.

They said one of the Palestinians was in hospital after being shot in the head during clashes between Israeli soldiers and about 200 high school students who blocked a main road near the northern West Bank town of Jenin and threw stones.
The other wounded boy was sent home after being treated at the Jenin hospital.
An Israeli army spokesman said students threw firebombs and stones at the Israelis who responded with teargas and rubber bullets. He had no knowledge of injuries.
In another incident on the outskirts of the PLO-ruled town, Palestinian police used force to prevent youths from hurling rocks at Israeli soldiers.

Palestinian stone-throwers have clashed almost daily with Israeli soldiers since Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu sent bulldozers to break ground on a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem on March 18.

One Palestinian university student was shot dead and hundreds were treated for tear gas inhalation and rubber bullet wounds during the confrontations which began in Hebron and Bethlehem areas and spread to other parts of the West Bank.
The Israeli army said it imposed a curfew on the al-Arroub refugee camp, also in the West Bank, following unrest there on Monday. There were no reports of casualties in the incident.
Earlier on Monday, the Israeli army demolished the home of a Palestinian suicide bomber who killed three Israeli women at a Tel Aviv cafe on March 21.
